correctness.rationale: For nonempty parts and r≥2 the two distinct-vertex distances are 1 across parts and 2 within each part (only 1 occurs when all parts are singletons). Thus p=0 leaves all sets, p=1 permits only sets in one part, and p≥2 restricts to at most one vertex. Independently d=0 requires V, d=1 permits exactly the sets meeting multiple parts or equal to a whole part, and d≥2 permits all nonempty sets. The generating function for sets meeting multiple parts is (1+x)^N−1−Σ_i((1+x)^{n_i}−1), disjoint from the whole-part contributions. Intersecting with the three packing filters gives all eight cases; the empty set is never feasible and V is invalid for d=0,p≥1 because an across-part pair exists. The smallest nonzero exponents match the second table, including no universal vertex when q=0 and all the infinite cases. A separate BFS and subset replay (python /workspace/branches/independent_reproduction.py 2) matched all cardinality coefficients on seven profiles, including cliques, singleton parts and profiles with none, for all 36 parameter pairs 0≤d,p≤5; the general result follows from the distance argument.
